labels.name: no-action

items.body:
### What do you want to change?

On exit pi shows some text to resume a session like this:

```
To resume this session: pi --session <id>
```

This change moves it to this format:

```
To resume this session:
pi --session <id>
```

### Why?

I caught this from Claude Code who has the resume command on a separate line.

With this change I can triple click the `pi --session <id>` line in my terminal and it selects the whole thing for a quick copy and paste so I can move it to a different tab or something.

With the single line version I have to use my mouse to highlight the the entire command, hopeing I don't miss a character, yes, i'm that lazy

This is a simple QoL improvement for a workflow I do often as I moved betwen windows

### How? (optional)

The change as a diff:

```diff
--- a/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts
+++ b/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts
-            process.stdout.write(`${chalk.dim("To resume this session:")} ${resumeCommand}\n`);
+            process.stdout.write(`${chalk.dim("To resume this session:")}\n${resumeCommand}\n`);
```

Happy to submit the PR with this change once approved.

items.title: feat(tui): add opt-in overlay selection exclusion
items.body:
## Motivation

Persistent extension UI — sidebars, HUDs, status rails — can only be mounted through the overlay lifecycle. While such an overlay is visible, Pi cannot assume the user wants transcript selection, so fullscreen copy falls back to the composed terminal screen. Everything the overlay painted ends up in the copied text, along with the scrollbar column and padding beside it.

The workaround has to be built out of TUI internals. Pi Atelier renders its Sidebar as a fullscreen `HStack` child and replaces `showOverlay`/`hideOverlay` on the TUI instance while reading the private `layoutRoot` field ([`src/split-pane.ts`](https://github.com/michaelmjhhhh/pi-atelier/blob/main/src/split-pane.ts)) — a large amount of adapter code whose only job is to keep the Sidebar out of copied text.

The related proposals — [#3769](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3769) (`ctx.ui.setSidePanel`) and [#4992](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/4992) (selection-safe persistent panels) — asked for a new layout primitive and are closed.

This PR adds a smaller seam instead: an overlay can declare that it is not part of selectable content. Pi then keeps selecting from the transcript's own content. No new layout API, and no extension reaching into TUI internals. Pi Atelier can fold its adapter into this in a follow-up.

## Changes

- add `OverlayOptions.selection` with `"normal"` and `"exclude"`; the default remains `"normal"`
- record the rendered screen regions of visible excluded overlays
- keep transcript `ScrollView` selection and scrollbar targeting available when every visible overlay is excluded
- prevent a selection from starting inside an excluded overlay
- snap a drag that enters an excluded region to the edge the pointer came from, so entering from the left no longer also selects the text underneath the overlay
- keep an in-progress selection drag attached to the pointer: an excluded overlay that handles mouse events no longer swallows its motion and release
- preserve the existing behavior whenever a normal visible overlay is present

## Scope

- `exclude` is a selection and copy policy only. The overlay still composites over the layout; it does not reserve a column or reflow the transcript.
- Only drags that start on selectable content are covered. A selection whose endpoints are both outside any `ScrollView` still reads the composed screen.
- Excluded overlays are not selectable themselves; the option means "not part of selectable content", not "selectable only on its own".
- No new side-panel layout API, and no change to overlay focus, visibility, or lifecycle semantics.
- fullscreen TUI selection only; regular mode continues to use terminal-native selection
- opt-in and backward compatible; existing overlays are unchanged

## Testing

- `node --test "packages/tui/test/**/*.test.ts"` — 971 tests, 970 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing on the branch)
- Three new regressions, on top of the existing excluded-overlay case: an excluded overlay covering the transcript, entered from both the left and the right; a press inside it while a selection already exists; and a mouse-handling (`MouseRegion`) excluded overlay during an in-progress drag
- Each new regression was verified to fail with its fix reverted
- `npm run check` — biome, pinned-deps, runtime-deps, ts-imports, entry-graphs and shrinkwrap checks pass. `tsgo --noEmit` stops on one pre-existing error in `packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts(402,10)`, which is present without these changes; nothing in `packages/tui` is reported.

items.title: fix(agent): parallel tool batches persist each sibling result on its own completion
items.body:
# fix(agent): parallel tool batches persist each sibling result on its own completion

## Summary

Restructure `executeToolCallsParallel` in `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` so that each sibling's `toolResultMessage` is persisted (emitted) at that sibling's own completion, never gated on the batch's `Promise.all` barrier. Add an abort race so the barrier can be abandoned when the user presses Esc, synthesizing "Operation aborted" outcomes for never-settled siblings so no tool call is orphaned.

## Root Cause

In the previous implementation, `createToolResultMessage` + `emitToolResultMessage` ran in a sequential loop **after** `await Promise.all(...)`. This meant:

1. `tool_execution_end` was emitted per sibling on completion (from #3503), but the toolResult message was not persisted until **all** siblings settled.
2. If one tool stalled (e.g. a network socket ignoring the abort signal), the `Promise.all` barrier never resolved.
3. While waiting, **no** toolResult was persisted to `Agent.state.messages` via `message_end` → `agent.ts::processEvents`.
4. On the next turn, `transformMessages` synthesised `isError: true "No result provided"` for every tool in the batch.
5. The UI appeared frozen because `turn_end`/`agent_end` were never reached.

## The Fix

### Per-sibling persistence
Each prepared tool call thunk now calls `createToolResultMessage` + `emitToolResultMessage` inline on its own completion, before resolving. Completed siblings can no longer be gated by a stalled sibling.

### Claim map
A `Map<toolCallId, ToolResultMessage>` coordinates emission with the abort race. Whoever inserts an id into the map is the one to emit that result. The check-before-insert never spans an `await`, so every `toolCallId` gets exactly one emitted `toolResult` — including when a stalled sibling settles after the batch was already abandoned on abort (it sees the claim and stays silent).

### Abort race
`Promise.race([allSettled, waitForAbort(signal)])` lets the function exit even when a sibling ignores the abort signal. On abort, `synthesizeAbortedOutcomes` builds error outcomes for any sibling that never settled (or whose thunk's emission was still in-flight), emitting `tool_execution_end` + `toolResult` for each so UIs clear their "running" state.

### Return-value semantics preserved
The returned `messages` array and `turn_end.toolResults` remain in assistant source order regardless of completion order, so downstream consumers and `shouldTerminateToolBatch` are unaffected.

## Behavior Change

**In parallel mode, `toolResult` message events (`message_start`/`message_end`) are now emitted in tool completion order** rather than assistant source order. `turn_end.toolResults` and the messages returned from the batch remain in assistant source order (matched by `toolCallId`). This mirrors the existing `tool_execution_end` completion-order semantics from #3503. Extensions and UIs that consume `toolResult` events should be updated accordingly.

## Files Changed

- `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` — restructured `executeToolCallsParallel`
- `packages/agent/src/types.ts` — updated `ToolExecutionMode` and `AgentLoopConfig.toolExecution` TSDoc
- `packages/agent/test/agent-loop.test.ts` — updated one existing test + 6 new regression tests
- `packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md` — updated `tool_execution_*` and `tool_result` documentation
- **Publishing setup** (same branch): renamed all `@earendil-works/*` packages to `@bramburn/*`, added `.npmrc` with `NPM_TOKEN` to each, added `.github/workflows/publish.yml` to publish on tag push

## Test Commands

```bash
# Run agent-loop tests (21 original + 6 new = 27 passing)
cd packages/agent && npx vitest --run test/agent-loop.test.ts

# Typecheck
cd .. && npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/agent/tsconfig.build.json
```

## Related Issues

Fixes #7053. Related to the broader `Promise.all`-barrier pattern: #7113, #6665, #7153, #6755.

items.title: [Windows] Alt-screen viewport jumps to top and keyboard input stops until the window is clicked

labels.name: no-action

items.body:
### What happened?

While pi is streaming output or running tool calls, the alt-screen viewport
sometimes jumps back to the top on its own. After that, keyboard input stops
working in the PowerShell tab. Nothing recovers input until I click inside the
Windows Terminal window with the mouse.

This is separate from the taskbar symptom in my earlier revision of this
report, which I am dropping: I could not find any default-enabled pi code path
that would move or flash the taskbar window. `terminal.setProgress` writes OSC
9;4 (packages/tui/src/terminal.ts:9-10, 532-547), but it defaults to off
(settings-manager.ts:1336), and the TUI writes no bare BEL. If the taskbar
behavior matters to anyone else, it needs its own report.

### Steps to reproduce

Environment: Windows 10 22H2, Windows Terminal 1.24.12741.0,
PowerShell 7.6.6, Node v24.12.0, pi 1.0.0.
Reproduced with `pi -ne`, so no extension is involved.

1. Open Windows Terminal, create a PowerShell tab.
2. Start pi.
3. Send one prompt that makes pi emit a long stream of output, for example
   write me a small sql database that is compatible with sqlite3
4. Watch the viewport while output is streaming.

I have not found a case where it does not happen

Still open, and I will fill these in as I go: whether it also happens in
conhost, and whether it depends on the window being resized or unfocused.

### Expected behavior

The viewport should not scroll to the top on its own, and keyboard input
should keep working without requiring a mouse click.

### Version

1.0.0

items.title: Anthropic tool calls: corrupted non-ASCII edit arguments are silently accepted (dropped `u` in `\uXXXX` → `\b`/`\f` control chars)
items.body:
### What happened?

With Claude models, `edit` calls on files containing Korean text fail very often, and occasionally corrupt a file. I have been tracking this for about three weeks. It keeps coming back and costs a lot of retries.

There are two symptoms, usually in the same sessions:

1. **Control characters instead of Korean.** The arguments contain C0 control characters where Korean characters were intended.
2. **Garbage calls.** An `edit` whose `oldText` is a few meaningless characters that exist nowhere in the file. Several in a row can occur.

Both usually fail safely as "Could not find ... oldText". Once, a corrupted `newText` was written to a file and had to be repaired by hand.

### The pattern behind symptom 1

It points to a `\uXXXX` escape whose `u` is missing in the tool-input JSON. When the next hex digit happens to be `b` or `f`, the result is still **valid JSON**: `\b` / `\f` followed by the remaining three hex digits. `JSON.parse` accepts it, so the tool runs with wrong strings instead of returning an error.

Illustration (synthetic): intended `\ub0b4` → emitted `\b0b4` → parsed as U+0008 + `0b4`.

### Evidence

Automated scan of my local session logs (edit arguments only, no file contents):

| Model | edit calls | errors | error rate | args with C0 control chars |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| openai-codex/gpt-6-astra | 398 | 9 | 2.3% | 0 |
| openai-codex/gpt-6-sol | 82 | 5 | 6.1% | 0 |
| xai/grok-4.7 | 27 | 3 | 11% | 0 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 | 212 | 86 | 40.6% | 15 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 34 | 20 | 58.8% | 8 |
| anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 | 20 | 8 | 40% | 2 |

- All control characters found in Claude edit arguments are U+0008 (`\b`) or U+000C (`\f`). 848 of 873 are followed by exactly three hex digits.
- An earlier manual classification over 20 days: 52 of 68 failed Opus 5.5 edits had lost their Korean text. GPT, Grok and DeepSeek had none.
- I found no case where `repairJson` turned an invalid escape into a literal backslash, so I don't think the repair path causes this. The corrupted cases are already valid JSON before any repair.

### What I ruled out

- **`eager_input_streaming`:** on vs off, 21 attempts each. One corrupted call in each group.
- **Session length:** I forked an affected session and ran four edits each with the default `edit`, a hash-anchored edit extension, and all extensions loaded. All 12 succeeded. On the same day, the original window failed 3 of 4.
- **Edit tool format:** the hash-anchored edit tool made no difference.
- **Encoding in general:** in the same failing window, shell edits, `write`, and a Node script inside the shell all wrote Korean correctly.

### A context effect

The failures cluster after corrupted strings have been visible in the context. In the original window, the broken calls closely resembled an example string that had just been displayed during analysis. Later, a fresh session reproduced it twice in a row right after reading notes that contained such an example. I also hit the garbage-call symptom about six times today in a long session, after the raw examples had already been removed from those notes, so removing them does not prevent it.

So this looks like a model-side tendency that feeds on its own output. I can't prove where the `u` goes missing from the client side.

### Why report it here

Even if the root cause is the model, the pi-side problem is that corruption is silent. A cheap guard would make it a normal retryable validation error:

- For `edit` / `write` (or any string tool args), reject C0 control characters other than `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, with a message like "argument contains control character U+0008; possible malformed \u escape".
- Or, in the Anthropic provider, flag `\b`/`\f` followed by hex digits in the raw `partialJson` before parsing.

If the context effect is real, the error should not echo the corrupted string back to the model. Naming the code point is probably enough.

I can write this guard as a local extension (a `tool_call` handler returning `{ block, reason }`). It seems worth handling in core, though, because every non-ASCII user on Claude is exposed to silent file corruption.

Related: #6278 (Claude tool-call schema errors, closed as model behavior). This case is narrower: non-ASCII content only, and it can corrupt files without any validation error.

### Steps to reproduce

Not deterministic. Using a Claude model, ask for several `edit` calls that replace Korean text in a UTF-8 file. It is much more likely once a corrupted string has appeared in the conversation. Failures show up as oldText mismatches whose arguments contain U+0008/U+000C, or as very short oldText values.

I can share the log-scanning script (counts only) if helpful.

### Version / environment

- pi 0.87.1 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Windows, PowerShell 7
- Provider `anthropic`, Claude subscription login through the third-party `@gotgenes/pi-anthropic-auth` 3.3.2 extension. It only handles authentication, but I have not tested with an API key.

items.title: Anthropic provider: use the SDK's workload identity federation env vars
items.body:
Closes #10177

With no key, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or stored credential configured, the anthropic provider now treats `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` as configuration and hands the bundled SDK a federation `config`. The SDK exchanges the identity token for a short-lived access token and refreshes it itself, so CI can run pi without a static key. `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` is passed through when set.

The resolver returns the ids in `env` (they're provider config, like the Cloudflare account ids), and `createClient` builds the SDK `config` from them with `apiKey` and `authToken` null so the SDK doesn't read a key from the environment on its own. Keys and tokens keep precedence, matching the SDK. Only the `anthropic` provider federates. No new dependency.

`npm run check` and `./test.sh` pass. Also verified in GitHub Actions against a real federation rule, with pi built from this branch: with the four variables set and no key present, requests succeed, and they keep succeeding after a background loop has replaced the identity token file.

items.title: Let extensions keep the session busy after agent_settled (OSC 7501 reports done too early)

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

items.body:
### What do you want to change?

A way for an extension to mark the session as still working after the turn ends, e.g. a counted `pi.holdBusy()` that returns a release function. While a hold is active, `ctx.isIdle()` stays false and the program status reporter keeps reporting `working`. `agent_settled` keeps firing as it does now.

### Why?

Extensions that run background work (subagents, long builds) end the turn and deliver results later as messages. Between those two points pi says it is done:

- since 1.1.0, `ProgramStatusReporter` turns `agent_settled` into OSC 7501 `done`, so a terminal or dashboard shows the pane as finished while three subagents are still running;
- `ctx.isIdle()` is true, so herdr's Pi hook reports idle too.

An extension can't fix this on its own: the reporter only listens to agent events, and without a session-level signal every integration would have to subscribe to a private "in flight" event from each extension.

Follow-up to #10451, which was auto-closed over a weekend. OSC 7501 now makes the gap visible in every terminal that supports it.

### How? (optional)

A counter on `AgentSession`: `isIdle` (`agent-session.ts:1465`) becomes `... && holds === 0`, `ExtensionAPI` gets `holdBusy()` returning a release function, and `ProgramStatusReporter` reports `working` while the count is above zero, then the run's outcome once it drops to zero. Happy to implement it if the shape works for you.

(Drafted with AI help; checked against v1.1.0.)

items.title: Support mcp over unix socket
items.body:
### What do you want to change?

Support MCP over Unix socket, adding `"socket": "/run/.../mcp.sock"` as a valid option to `mcp.json`


### Why?

Currently, only stdio and http are supported:
- `stdio`: requires the executable (and credentials) to be mounted to the namespace containing pi; agents with read tool can inspect it.
- http: requires exposing a port then mapped to the namespace containing pi, all users have access to said port unless additional firewall is added.

A third option, is to bind a unix socket to the namespace containing pi; the mcp is spawn on its own namespace, and the stdio over unix socket is the only tunnel between the namespaces.
This allows, for example, 0 credentials binded to the pi namespace.

Example systemd services:

`units-mcp.service`
```
[Unit]
Description=Units MCP socket
Requires=units-mcp.socket
After=units-mcp.socket

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/true
RemainAfterExit=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

`units-mcp.socket`
```
[Unit]
Description=Units MCP Unix socket

[Socket]
ListenStream=%t/units-mcp/mcp.sock
SocketMode=0600
DirectoryMode=0700
Accept=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=sockets.target
```

`units-mcp@.service`
```
[Unit]
Description=Units MCP connection (%i)

[Service]
ExecStart=%h/.local/share/mcp/venv/units/bin/systemd-units-mcp --home "%h/.local/share/namespaces/home/pi-sandbox/0"
StandardInput=socket
StandardOutput=socket
StandardError=journal

UMask=0077
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
Restart=no
[ good'old systemd hardening options ]
```

### How? (optional)

This mode is implemented on 
https://pi.dev/packages/pi-mcp-adapter

should add ~170 lines with tests based on pi (gpt-sol) implemented on itself

### Use cases

Once you deferred the sandboxing responsibilities to systemd, you can do cool stuff, for example, have the stdio over ssh; no need to bring your own authentication if you need to share between machines. A server app, without a client!

items.title: Let the Anthropic provider use the SDK's workload identity federation env vars
items.body:
### What do you want to change?

When `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` are set (and no API key or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN), have the built-in anthropic provider hand authentication to the bundled Anthropic SDK, which already implements the OIDC token exchange and refresh for exactly those variables.

### Why?

We run pi in GitHub Actions. Our CI authenticates to Anthropic with Workload Identity Federation (WIF) – short-lived tokens from the job's OIDC token, no stored API key. Since pi already bundles the `@anthropic-ai/sdk` SDK that already supports this from the env vars above, including refresh, but pi never lets it run: the provider always resolves a key or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` itself and constructs the client with an explicit `apiKey`/`authToken`. 

(It can be worked around with `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` plus a `models.json` header `!command` that reads a token file we rotate in the background. It works, but makes things complicated than necessary.)

### How? (optional)

In `providers/anthropic.ts`, add one more fallback at the end of `resolve()`: if the four federation env vars are set, return an auth object with no `apiKey` and no `headers`, just a flag (something like `auth: { sdkManaged: true }`) that tells the client code not to inject a credential itself. Keys and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` keep winning, so nothing changes unless you set all four.

In `anthropic-messages.ts`, when `createClient()` sees `sdkManaged`, it builds the client without passing `apiKey` or `authToken`, so the SDK's own credential logic runs (it does the exchange and refreshes from the identity token file on its own). `assertRequestAuth()` needs to allow `sdkManaged` too.

Plus a line in `docs/providers.md` and a couple of resolver tests. No new deps, the bundled SDK already supports it.

items.title: RPC: no way to clear queued steering/followUp messages (abort keeps the queues)
items.body:
Hi! I maintain [pi-courier](https://github.com/Hi-Barry/pi-courier), a Matrix bridge that drives pi through `--mode rpc`. While implementing an "interrupt and redirect" command for remote users I hit a queue semantics gap in the RPC surface, and I wanted to check whether this is intentional before assuming it's an oversight.

**What I observed**

In `AgentSession`, `abort()` only aborts the active run — `_steeringMessages` and `_followUpMessages` survive, and get delivered on the next run. That's coherent on its own, and the TUI makes it work nicely: on Esc it calls `clearQueue()` first, puts the queued text back into the editor, *then* aborts (`restoreQueuedMessagesToEditor({ abort: true })`). So the interactive user always sees and re-edits what was queued.

Through the RPC surface there's no equivalent of that flow:

- the `abort` command maps to plain `session.abort()` — the queues survive;
- there's no `clear_queue` command (or a `clearQueue` option on `abort`) in `rpc-mode.js`;
- the RPC client does receive `queue_update` events, so it *knows* messages are pending, but has no way to do anything about them.

**Why this matters for headless clients**

A typical remote interaction is "stop what you're doing, do this instead". With the current RPC surface the old steering/followUp messages stay queued, so after abort + a new prompt, the stale messages get injected into the new run — exactly what the user was trying to cancel. The TUI avoids this only because it clears the queues client-side before aborting; every other RPC client is left to work around it (I currently surface a "queue still contains N messages" warning instead, which is honest but not great).

**Possible directions** (no preference, just what I could think of):

1. add a `clear_queue` command to the RPC protocol, possibly returning what was dropped (the TUI already restores it to the editor, so other clients would probably want the text too);
2. or an optional flag on the `abort` command (`clearQueue?: boolean`);
3. or document the current behavior as intended so clients know to build around it.

Happy to put up a PR if you think this belongs in the protocol — it looks like a small change, but I'd rather align on the shape first.
